ship_of_the_week.subject: fix(automation): stop cowork-auto-sync loop from rewriting 6 files every commit

session_focus.summary: Retro-driven fix session: root-caused and fixed the self-regenerating pre-commit/cowork-auto-sync loop that 3 consecutive prior retros flagged as an unfixed 2-week pattern (SKILLPACK-*.md/json, dashboard.html, audit/COWORK-*.md rewriting every commit regardless of content change). Fix touched 5 generator scripts: added a Write-IfChanged content-diff guard (skips writes when output is identical modulo embedded timestamps) at all 8 write sites, added missing loop guards to 3 of 5 generators that lacked them, and fixed a real PowerShell hashtable-enumeration nondeterminism bug that was silently defeating any diff check. Verified stable across 4 consecutive live runs before committing. Also triaged a weekly-session-audit report: corrected 2 overstated governance claims in CLAUDE.md (a nonexistent roadmap-scan doc/CI job, and an overstated Tier-1-approved marketplace-spec status that's actually still an unsigned template), logged 4 uncaptured 2026-08-01 fix commits to memory, and logged 3 retro-pipeline data-quality bugs (metric-unit convention silently switched fraction->percent mid-series, window field mislabeled 7d on 1-day-span files, backlog trending up not down) to TODOS.md since the root cause lives in the external /retro gstack plugin, not this repo.
incidents: RESOLVED this session: self-regenerating pre-commit validator hooks, a 2-week pattern per 2026-08-02-1.json and 2026-08-02-2.json (9-11 touches/file/week). Root cause was two-fold: (1) all 5 generator scripts unconditionally Set-Content'd fresh ISO timestamps every run with no diff check, and (2) only 2 of 5 had loop guards, so nested calls re-ran siblings redundantly. A real nondeterminism bug (unsorted PowerShell hashtable .Keys enumeration shuffling the sync-log order every run) was also found and fixed -- it would have defeated even a correct diff-check. Verified via 4 live reruns: steady-state output is now byte-identical modulo timestamps.

bulk_sync_commit 4f66345f (12767 ins, dated 07-26) is the 4th consecutive retro to flag the same commit as a hotspot/LOC distortion -- decision made this session to leave it untagged (retroactive chore(sync) retag doesn't fix already-computed historical metrics) and just enforce the convention going forward.

Backlog (TODOS.md open items) grew 10 -> 16 same-day, driven partly by this session's own additions (3 retro-pipeline findings, plus externally-added trm-sync-treatment follow-up items from a concurrent session). Net backlog growth outpacing closure is now visible across 2 consecutive same-day snapshots -- worth a dedicated burn-down pass.

A CI failure screenshot was shared for a different, unrelated repo (sorensencc-dotcom/cic-os) -- diagnosed as pre-existing package-lock.json/package.json drift unrelated to the failing PR's actual diff (a CLAUDE.md doc-only change). Not fixed: no local clone of that repo in this session.
process_learnings: A diff-check that only strips timestamps is insufficient if the underlying data structure iterates in nondeterministic order (PowerShell hashtable .Keys) -- the shuffled-but-content-identical output looks like a real diff every time. Sort before iterating whenever loop output feeds a stability check.

When a git hook triggers a sub-process that itself regenerates tracked files (pre-commit's Gate 3 running the full validator chain), expect one settling commit after the first real fix lands, before steady-state holds. Don't mistake that one-time settle for the fix not working.

Governance doc claims (CLAUDE.md 'CI is authoritative', 'Tier 1 approved') should be checked against the actual referenced artifact (workflow schedule triggers, SUCCESS.md signature block) before being trusted or built against -- both flagged claims in this session were stale by weeks, not days.
